contractSource: Description: "Generate secure and easy WiFi passwords..." The page shows "Password Strength", "Entropy (bits)" and "Estimated Crack Time" for the generated password; option "Memorable (Easy to type)".
groundTruth: The entropy of a generated password is set by how it was generated, not by which character classes happen to appear in it: log2(number of equally likely outputs). A letter drawn from 21 consonants carries log2 21 = 4.39 bits, from 5 vowels log2 5 = 2.32 bits, a digit log2 10 = 3.32 bits; a fixed separator carries none.

cases.derivation: A 12-character memorable password is built as an alternating consonant/vowel run (6 letters: 3 × 4.39 + 3 × 2.32 = 20.1 bits), about 2–4 digits (6.6–13.3 bits), a fixed '-' (0 bits) and a short second run (≈ 4.4 bits): roughly 31–38 bits, so 40 ± 10 bits bounds it generously. Scoring it as 12 random characters from a 70-symbol set (12 × log2 70 ≈ 74 bits) overstates it by more than 30 bits — about 10 billion times.
